question: True or false: early maps showed California as an island because Spanish sailors had not yet explored its gulf?
answer: False. Francisco de Ulloa sailed to the head of the Gulf of California in 1539, and for some 80 years most maps drew Baja California as a peninsula. The island appeared in the 1620s and was copied from map to map for over a century; Ferdinand VI decreed in 1747 that California was no island.
move: Knowledge can go backwards; ask whether an error came before the truth or after.
trap: Assuming maps only ever improve, so an error means nobody had looked.
reference: McLaughlin & Mayo, The Mapping of California as an Island: An Illustrated Checklist, California Map Society Occasional Paper No. 5, 1995
